Agents Learn to Reason, Robots Master Control

Today's papers reveal a field in motion: AI agents are gaining sophistication in reasoning and long-horizon planning, while robotics is shifting toward compact, interpretable policies. The standout theme is multimodal integration—vision-language models grounding abstract reasoning in physical and visual reality—paired with a parallel push for efficiency, from subquadratic attention mechanisms to edge-deployable systems.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
Robotics
Compact world models unlock precise robot control

La-JEPA demonstrates that robot policies don't need massive generation-oriented transformers—training directly in latent feature space yields competitive control with far fewer parameters. This challenges the prevailing assumption that bigger architectures automatically translate to better robot behavior.

Latent Action JEPA achieves control comparable to large world-action models while requiring significantly fewer parameters and lower inference costs.
Clémente, Xue, Abyaneh 2611.08156 PDF
Machine Learning
Subquadratic attention scales vision transformers beyond limits

SSoG replaces dense self-attention with learned mixtures of axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, dropping complexity from O(N²) to subquadratic while maintaining global Lipschitz continuity. This opens doors for vision transformers to process much higher resolutions without the quadratic memory wall.

Separable sum-of-Gaussians operators reduce Vision Transformer cost per layer from quadratic to subquadratic token complexity while guaranteeing convergence properties via Picard-Lindelöf theorem.
Boned Riera, Romero Sanchez, Ramos Terrades 2611.08236 PDF
Computer Vision
Medical 3D scans decoded by hierarchical mixture-of-experts

MedHiVE introduces hierarchical Soft Mixture-of-Experts for medical vision-language models, routing both vision and text tokens through anatomy-aware layers. This structure mirrors how doctors reason—focusing on specific anatomical regions before integrating global context—making the model both more accurate and more interpretable.

MedHiVE is the first framework to systematically organize both vision and text token routing through anatomical hierarchy in medical vision-language models.
Mert, Płotka, Bassi 2611.08185 PDF
AI Safety
Multimodal social engineering reveals agent security gaps

Multimodal-SEA benchmarks AI agents against 152 real-world fraud attack scenarios combining text, image, and video. Current agents fail significantly under coordinated multimodal attacks, exposing a critical blind spot in deployment-ready systems that must resist sophisticated deception.

Personal AI agents show substantial vulnerability to multimodal social engineering attacks, with current systems failing to consistently verify forged content across modalities.
He, Zhang, Han 2611.08281 PDF
